title: Blullant Move!?!
transcript: You know when you think you play the brilliant move, and then you open the game review and see that it's actually a blunder? Well, I have a great example of that for you. I was playing this game. This is a blitz online game, and I had just recaptured the pawn with my rook. The opponent attacks my knight with knight to h5. And here I spotted a beautiful idea. I traded the rooks and then played the brilliant rook to f7, leaving my queen to hang, and hanging my rook at the same time. But neither of these pieces can be taken. If you take the queen, this is going to be a checkmate in just one move. And if you take the rook, this is going to be another checkmate in two moves. So in the game, my opponent simply moved the rook away. I saved my queen, and I went on to win the game. So imagine my surprise when I opened the game review, thinking that I was going to make a video about this beautiful move, only to see that rook to f7 is actually a blunder. And I thought, "Well, this can't be. What can black possibly have in this position?" But as it turns out, black has queen to c1. And after I move my king to h2, imagine my shock when I saw that the only winning move for black, and the move that would have turned the tables for my opponent, is the brilliant and disgusting queen to h1. Queen to h1? Like you you must be kidding me. Queen to h1 is a ridiculous move to play, and a move that I would have had to foresee from this position to avoid losing. And the idea is that queen to h1, of course, has to be taken. The king cannot go anywhere. But now we have lured the king into position where black can recapture the white queen with a check. The king comes back up, and now the rook falls, and it doesn't matter that you win the knight back. Black has a rook for a bishop and is completely winning. Chess never stops to amaze me, and I wait for the day that I'll find a move like this myself.
